title: As Iran’s oil lifeline runs dry, can it outlast Trump's economic siege?
gist: Iran's crude stockpiled outside the reach of the US naval blockade has fallen to zero, all discharged in China, about two months into the US sanctions-plus-blockade campaign; it is unclear whether the pain forces concessions or escalation.

insights.claim: Iran's oil on water outside the US blockade fell to zero as of last week, with all volumes discharged in China, according to Kpler.
insights.speaker: Samuel Wendel
insights.so_what: Removes Iranian floating-storage supply from the Chinese market; watch Chinese teapot refiner feedstock and discounts on alternative sour barrels.
insights.quote: Iran's oil on water outside the blockade has fallen to zero as of last week, and all volumes have been discharged in China

insights.claim: Kpler's head of crude oil analysis says this is the first time Iran has faced such a challenge in its modern history.
insights.speaker: Samuel Wendel
insights.so_what: Unprecedented export squeeze raises the odds of regime economic stress.
insights.quote: This is the first time Iran has faced such a challenge in its modern history.

insights.claim: The milestone comes roughly two months into Operation Economic Outcast, a US sanctions campaign backed by a maritime blockade aimed at depriving Iran of revenue for its government and war effort.
insights.speaker: Samuel Wendel
insights.so_what: Blockade-plus-sanctions is the operative policy; track enforcement and any easing signals.

insights.claim: Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent predicted on Sept. 27 that Iran would complete remaining oil deliveries within two weeks, leaving Tehran with nothing left to trade.
insights.speaker: Samuel Wendel
insights.so_what: The prediction has played out; next question is Tehran's response.
insights.quote: nothing left to trade for anything

insights.claim: It is uncertain whether mounting financial pain will force Iranian concessions or intensify the conflict as both sides continue saber-rattling.
insights.speaker: Samuel Wendel
insights.so_what: Two-sided tail risk: negotiation versus escalation affecting oil and Gulf risk.

insights.claim: Shops in Tehran's Tajrish Bazaar sit mostly empty with few customers, illustrating the economic distress inside Iran.
insights.speaker: Samuel Wendel
insights.so_what: Anecdotal evidence of demand collapse; monitor unrest and rial indicators.
